claims.text: A neural-network machine-learning interatomic potential trained on ab initio molecular-dynamics snapshots from liquid and solid states near melting is proposed as the reference potential for CoCrFeMnNi.
The proposed MLIP will be more accurate than static EAM reference potentials for CoCrFeMnNi.
The MLIP will capture the complex many-body interactions present in the ab initio liquid.
Capturing these many-body interactions will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD using static EAM references.
CoCrFeMnNi configurations from approximately 0.8Tm to Tm include both liquid and solid atomic configurations with extensive many-body interactions.
An active-learning loop will ensure coverage of the relevant near-melting configuration space.
The simulations will be conducted at constant pressure over approximately 0.8Tm to Tm.
Training and prediction over approximately 0.8Tm to Tm will cover the breadth of configurations encountered near and at melting.
Local atomic descriptors such as symmetry functions or bispectrum components can capture many-body effects and distinguish diverse local environments.
Learning directly from ab initio molecular-dynamics data will improve representation of the liquid-state energetic landscape.
A more faithful liquid-state energetic landscape will improve reference-target phase-space overlap.
Continuous representation of many-body correlations will narrow the thermodynamic-integration path difference relative to standard EAM references.
The MLIP will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 40–50% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The MLIP will yield free-energy predictions within 20 meV/atom of direct ab initio calculations.
TOR-TILD static EAM potentials typically produce liquid-state free-energy errors exceeding 20 meV/atom for high-entropy alloys.
The proposed approach is applicable specifically to CoCrFeMnNi from approximately 0.8Tm to Tm.
Application outside the specified temperature interval or to significantly different alloy systems may require additional training and validation.
Incomplete sampling of rare or extreme configurations may limit MLIP performance.
The MLIP may not transfer fully across slight compositional variations within the CoCrFeMnNi system.
The hypothesis is falsified if free-energy error exceeds 20 meV/atom relative to an ab initio benchmark or path-mismatch improvement is less than 40% relative to TOR-TILD EAM.
